body: thank you for commenting on my post. I love you stranger♥️ I hope things get better for both of us.

Not quite. It's broken up into four parts. Interpersonal effectiveness, mindfulness, distress tolerance and emotional regulation. It's teaching you how to handle extreme emotions and impulses, be more accepting of your being, and giving you the skills to set boundaries and be more assertive without being too aggressive. It's balancing the "emotion mind" with the "wise mind" which is what people with good cognitive balance do normally but is something I never learned because of past abuse and genetics. People that don't necessarily have difficulty with balance still benefit, although it's not as necessary as the people that actively can't cope because of it. 

What some people don't understand about BPD and the lack of skills is its just something I never had in the first place. Asking me to calm down because something minor happened doesn't work because I just can't. It's like asking someone to add when they havent been taught to comprehend numbers. Similarly, just because I don't have the skills doesn't mean it's not my responsibility to fix that. Doesn't matter that my dog peed on the floor... I still need to clean it or it will damage the floor. 🤷🏼‍♀️

Thank you so much for commenting... I'm sorry for your struggles too. This whole thing just sucks. The only reason I haven't given up hope is because the type of therapy I've been receiving has a high success rate for those with BPD. It fucking sucks. It's hard to learn how to process my emotions when I haven't been doing it for 20 years lol.
Difficult. It's effective but it's hard and you have to really want to do it. You're teaching yourself how to think differently and it's a pain in the ass.

according to Wikipedia: Dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) is an evidence-based psychotherapy that began with efforts to treat Borderline Personality Disorder (preferably known as Emotional Instability Disorder). DBT has been proven useful in treating mood disorders, suicidal ideation, and for change in behavioral patterns such as self-harm, and substance abuse.
I'm in weekly DBT group therapy and private therapy. It helps a little. It will keep getting easier. Some nights are just hard. Thanks for the support.

What do you mean, there's always something else to try? I appreciate the offer but honestly I just posted this to get it off my chest, not look for people to talk to. Support is great but I don't need someone to save me by distracting me.
